manual_seed_payload.core_question: Do strict queue-realistic fills of unusually favorable late passive orders occur often enough, and do the filled subset win often enough after settlement and friction, to have positive expected value?
manual_seed_payload.origin_context: Short-duration Kalshi weather/rain markets motivated leaving unusually favorable passive limit orders rather than paying near-certain 97-99 cent prices.
manual_seed_payload.proof_of_mechanism: Confirmed historical example: Miami hourly-temperature 76F-or-above NO, resting 5 NO at 89 cents, full unexpected fill around 22:58, final settlement NO, cost $4.45, payout $5.00, realized profit +$0.55 (~12.36% ROI). This is not proof of edge.
required_kill_tests: profitability only under optimistic fill assumptions

next_decisive_test: Freeze and run a read-only prospective shadow protocol for late passive maker orders using conservative price-time queue reconstruction, sequence/reconnect/restart fail-closed handling, partial-fill accounting, post-fill markouts, authoritative final settlement and net EV after fees/friction. Keep optimistic fill assumptions outside PRIMARY results.
open_question: Discovery must read the manual seed, classify the mechanism without assuming a domain in advance, and identify the cheapest decisive falsification path.
provenance_note: User-supplied lead. Do not represent it as autonomously discovered by a scout.
queue_reason: Discovery and Mechanics now agree on a testable microstructure/settlement mechanism, but no prospective queue-realistic sample exists yet and adverse selection remains unmeasured.
